title: SLO Forensics: KV-cache & tail-latency runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a forensic runbook for SLO degradations where the dominant symptom is elevated tail latency (p95/p99) that correlates with KV-cache (prefix/KV) behavior. It covers metric definitions, tracing/span design to capture the relevant signals, dashboard layout recommendations, and a step-by-step investigation checklist. Intended readers: oncall, engineers triaging rollouts, and product reliability owners.

Summary of hypothesis space (quick triage):
- Cold prefixes / low prefix warmth -> more KV lookups causing increased CPU/GPU stalls.
- KV-cache eviction storms after memory pressure/batch changes -> transient p99 spikes.
- Batching policy shifts (larger batches) interacting with long sequence variance -> higher tail latency for long sequences.
- Model variant fallbacks (smaller/quantized kernels chosen) causing kernel-switch overheads under heavy routing/fallback.
- Network stalls between router and worker (rare, but visible as stage-level latency).

Canonical metrics to instrument (names we use internally):
- inference.request.count (counter, labels: tenant, route, model_id, model_variant)
- inference.request.latency_ms.histogram (buckets: [1,5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000]; labels: tenant, route, model_id, seq_length_bin, batch_size_bin, kvcache_hit)
- inference.request.latency_ms.p50/p95/p99 (derived from histogram)
- inference.kvcache.checks (counter, labels: tenant, model_id, prefix_key_hash_bucket)
- inference.kvcache.hit.count and inference.kvcache.miss.count (counters, labels: tenant, model_id, prefix_length_bin)
- inference.kvcache.hit_rate (gauge, computed: hits / (hits+misses) per 1m window)
- inference.kvcache.eviction.count (counter, labels: reason, model_id)
- inference.kvcache.size_bytes (gauge, per-model shard)
- inference.kvcache.prefix_warmth_ratio (gauge: fraction of requests hitting top-N prefixes)
- inference.batch.size.dist (histogram, labels: model_id, route)
- inference.queue.inflight_requests (gauge)
- inference.gpu.kernel_switch.count (counter, labels: kernel_id, reason)
- infra.gpu.utilization_pct and infra.gpu.sm_stall_ms (for stalls)
- routing.fallback.rate (counter/gauge: fraction of requests routed to fallback model_variant)
- deployment.rollout.event (event metric / audit log index)
- network.rpc.latency_ms per stage (gateway->router, router->worker)

Tracing / span design (anchors and required tags):
Required high-level spans for every request (order):
- span: client.request (client -> api-gateway)
- span: api.gateway -> router (attach route, tenant, request_id)
- span: router.dispatch (annotate chosen model_id, model_variant, batch_id)
- span: worker.kvcache_lookup (attach prefix_key_hash_bucket, prefix_length, hit:boolean, latency_ms)
- span: worker.batch_assemble (labels: batch_size, seq_lengths_summary)
- span: worker.model_inference (labels: model_id, variant, kernel_id, token_count, gpu_assigned)
- span: gpu.kernel_execution (labels: kernel_id, op_type, duration_ms)
- span: response.marshalling (size_bytes)
Span tags (must exist on all traces): request_id, tenant_id, route, model_id, model_variant, kvcache_hit (true|false), prefix_length, batch_id, batch_size, seq_length, seq_length_bin, kernel_id, stage_latency_ms.
Sampling rules (budget aware):
- Always sample 100% of requests that hit p99 latency threshold (server-side deterministic check: if overall request latency > p99 threshold for last 5m).
- Stratified sample: 1% global, 10% for tenants that exceed their error/latency SLO, 100% for tenants with enterprise_tier=true and >x SLO burn.
- Retain 100% of traces with kvcache.eviction events or kernel_switch events.

Dashboard layout (panels and recommended queries):
Top row: SLO + burn
- Panel: SLO status line (p95 latency vs SLO target), current burn rate, error budget left (1h/6h/24h windows).
- Query: derived p95 from inference.request.latency_ms.histogram filtered by service/route.

Second row: tail-latency decomposition
- Panel: p50/p95/p99 heatmap by seq_length_bin vs batch_size_bin (show baseline vs now).
- Panel: stacked time series showing kvcache.hit_rate (%) (per-model) and p99 latency overlay.
- Panel: scatter plot: prefix_warmth_ratio (x) vs p99 latency (y) per tenant (use jitter).

Third row: KV-cache signals and evictions
- Panel: kvcache.hit/miss counts (stacked) and hit_rate (line).
- Panel: kvcache.eviction.count by reason (OOM, TTL, manual) with spike annotation.
- Panel: kvcache.size_bytes and top-10 prefix key size distribution (bar).

Fourth row: Tracing + stage breakdown
- Panel: waterfall/stacked latency by stage (kvcache_lookup, batch_assemble, model_inference, kernel_execution).
- Panel: histogram of worker.kvcache_lookup latency to reveal long-tail lookup stalls.
- Panel: count of kernel_switch events and recent kernel ids (table).

Fifth row: Operational knobs and capacity
- Panel: batch.size.dist (percentiles) and inflight_requests; annotate autoscale events.
- Panel: gpu.utilization_pct and sm_stall_ms.
- Panel: routing.fallback.rate and model_variant_routing percentages.

Alert guidance (recommended thresholds):
- P95 latency above SLO target AND p99 > 2x SLO target for 5m -> P1/alert for SLO burn.
- kvcache.eviction.count spikes > 5x baseline in 1m -> P2 alert (investigate memory pressure/rollout).
- kvcache.hit_rate drops by >20 percentage points vs trailing 30m baseline AND p99 increases -> P1.
- kernel_switch.count spike > 50 events/min -> P2 (indicates unstable variant routing).

Investigation checklist (ordered):
1) Confirm scope: which tenants/routes/models are above SLO? start with the SLO status panel and time range 15m/1h/6h.
2) Correlate p99 spikes with kvcache metrics: check hit_rate, eviction spikes, size_bytes. If hit_rate low -> cold prefixes.
3) Open traces for a set of p99 requests (use the trace panel sampling rule): look for which stage dominates. If worker.kvcache_lookup dominates, inspect prefix_length and hit boolean tags.
4) For batch-related tails: inspect batch_size bins and seq_length distribution. Large variance -> long sequences pushing batch latency. Consider temporary per-route batch caps.
5) Check routing/fallbacking: routing.fallback.rate (did lots of requests fall back to another variant?). If so, look for kernel_switch events and kernel_id mismatches.
6) Check recent config/deployments: filter deployment.rollout.event stream for anything touching kvcache settings, memory, or batcher.
7) Check infra signals: GPU stalls, SM stalls, host OOM, network rpc latency spikes.
8) If eviction storm suspected: identify top prefixes evicted and determine if eviction policy (LRU vs TTL) is misconfigured.
9) Remediation actions (fast):
   - Temporarily lower per-route max_batch_size or enable fast-path small-batch mode.
   - Increase KV-cache memory quota for the affected model shard if possible (short-term bump).
   - Switch routing to a stable model_variant manually if kernel_switch storms are seen.
   - Rollback recent rollout if evidence points to new model_variant or runtime change.
10) Postmortem artifacts: attach sampled traces (p99), a time-annotated screenshot of the SLO dashboard, kvcache eviction list, and a short hypothesis->test->fix log.

Instrumentation gaps & short-term engineering tasks:
- Add prefix_key_length and kvcache_hit boolean as explicit tags to every span (if not present).
- Emit an event metric when the kvcache eviction rate per-shard exceeds threshold (easy to alert).
- Add per-tenant prefix_warmth_ratio to allow targeted investigations without sampling heavy traces.
- Emit kernel_switch.reason label (route change vs fallback vs configuration) for faster triage.
- If traces are large, add a compact trace view that only shows stage latencies and the 6 required tags (request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, batch_id, kvcache_hit, kernel_id).

Operational notes & caveats:
- Don’t assume low global hit_rate implies poor cache design; tail behavior can be driven by a small number of cold prefixes used by high-value tenants. Always check per-tenant prefix_warmth_ratio.
- Batching improvements can reduce cost but increase tail latency for long-tailed sequence distributions — prefer per-route batch tuning rather than global batch changes.
- Kernel switch events are noisy during multi-variant rollouts; correlate with rollout.event timestamps before escalating.

Quickplay examples (CLI snippets & dashboard links):
- Query p99 latency for route foo-app: 
  PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_ms_bucket{route="/v1/generate", model_id="m-compact"}[5m])) by (le))
- Top eviction prefixes (placeholder): 
  LogQL: topk(20, sum by(prefix_key_hash)(increase(inference_kvcache_eviction_count[15m])))
- Trace link example (replace REQUEST_ID): 
  https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/REQUEST_ID

Open questions / follow-ups:
- We need a concise definition of "prefix" for customers and instrumentation so that prefix_length bins are meaningful across models. Who owns the customer-facing doc? (assign to product-APIs).
- Should we add a per-tenant warmup probe (synthetic) for high-traffic tenants to reduce cold-prefix p99s? (experiment idea).
- What cost impact analysis should be required for an operational change that increases kvcache size quotas? (coordinate with finance).

Appendix: example thresholds we used in experiments (tune per workload)
- p99 SLO trigger: depends on route; common values: 800ms (interactive), 2000ms (batch infer).
- kvcache.hit_rate alert: absolute < 60% OR drop > 20 percentage points vs 30m median.
- eviction spike detection: > 5x 1h baseline or > 100 evictions/min.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and operator-focused rather than a full design doc. Please flag missing metrics that you rely on during oncall or any incompatible label names with your instrumented pipelines.
